ListRecursionDepth: How deeply list operations may process nested lists. Lowering the limit can stop unexpectedly deep input sooner.
DisplayMode: The number display style. Choose Std, Fix, Sci, Eng or Sig instead of entering a raw mode ID.
DisplayDigits: The digit count used by the current display style. Fix counts decimal places; the other styles use their documented digit convention.
StandardExponent: The exponent threshold at which standard display switches notation.
Precision: How many significant decimal digits calculations use. This affects arithmetic precision; Fix only changes displayed decimal places. For example, enter 16 Precision.
MinimumSignificantDigits: The minimum significant-digit count used by standard number display.
MantissaSpacing: How decimal mantissa digits are grouped for reading.
FractionSpacing: How fraction digits are grouped for reading.
BasedSpacing: How based-integer digits are grouped for reading.
AngleMode: The trigonometric angle unit. Choose Deg, Rad, Grad or PiRadians; those names need no stack argument.
CommandDisplayMode: How calculator command names are capitalized or expanded. Use the named command-display choices rather than raw IDs.
NameDisplayMode: How symbolic names are displayed. Use the named symbol-display choices rather than raw IDs.
Base: The radix used for generic based integers, from 2 to 36. Bin, Oct, Dec and Hex choose common bases without a numeric argument; on LumaRPL those commands also convert an ordinary decimal integer or a fixed-base integer at the top to the selected display base. Ctrl+Y opens Bases.
NumberSeparatorCommand: The separator between groups of decimal digits. Choose NumberSpaces, NumberDotOrComma, NumberTicks or NumberUnderscore.
BasedSeparatorCommand: The separator between groups of based-integer digits. Choose BasedSpaces, BasedDotOrComma, BasedTicks or BasedUnderscore.
WordSize: The bit width used by fixed-width based-number operations. This matters for shifts, rotations and signed interpretation.
MaxNumberBits: The largest integer bit size the engine allows.
MaxFlags: The number of numbered user flags available to RPL programs.
MaxRewrites: The iteration limit for symbolic rewriting, so a rewrite cannot continue indefinitely.
FractionIterations: How many iterations fraction conversion may try.
FractionLargestPrime: The prime-search limit used during fraction conversion.
FractionDigits: The digit limit used when converting a value to a fraction, rather than a display-decimal setting.
SolverIterations: The engine root solver's iteration limit. Guided workbench solving sets its own bounded solver context.
SolverImprecision: The precision allowance used by the engine root solver.
SolverShuffles: The shuffle allowance used by the numerical solver when seeking a solution.
IntegrationIterations: How many numerical integration refinements the engine may attempt.
IntegrationImprecision: The precision allowance used by engine numerical integration.
MaximumDecimalExponent: The allowed decimal exponent magnitude. Changing it does not create more memory for large numbers.
FinanceRounding: The rounding-digit setting for engine finance calculations. The native Financial calculator uses the conventions in its own Help.
MaxFactorsBits: The largest integer bit size accepted by the engine factorization operation.
MaxFactorIterations: The work limit for integer factorization.
MaxPolynomialDegree: The polynomial degree limit for engine polynomial processing.
MaxLaguerreIterations: The iteration limit for the Laguerre polynomial-root method.
MaxRootDivisor: The divisor-search limit used by polynomial-root processing.
MaxNameChainLength: How many chained name lookups the engine may follow.
MaxCallRecursion: How deeply RPL programs may call other programs recursively.
MaxStackDepth: The permitted calculator stack depth. Raising this limit does not enlarge the calculator arena.
MenuAppearance: The calculator soft-menu row layout. Choose SingleRowMenus, ThreeRowsMenus or FlatMenus rather than a raw layout ID.
LineWidth: The thickness, in pixels, for engine RPL drawing lines. Native interactive plots have separate controls.
CursorBlinkRate: The calculator-entry cursor blink interval in milliseconds.
CustomHeaderRefresh: The engine custom-header refresh interval in milliseconds.
BusyIndicatorRefresh: The engine busy-indicator refresh interval in milliseconds.
BatteryRefresh: The engine battery polling interval in milliseconds.
MinimumBatteryVoltage: A saved compatibility threshold from the original hardware. PicoCalc uses controller battery percentage for its safety check, not this voltage value.
GraphingTimeLimit: The engine object-graphing time limit in milliseconds. Native plot sampling uses its own work budgets.
ShowTimeLimit: How long the engine SHOW operation may spend rendering, in milliseconds.
ResultGraphingTimeLimit: The time allowed for graphically rendering a calculator result, in milliseconds.
StackGraphingTimeLimit: The time allowed for graphically rendering a stack object, in milliseconds.
TextRenderingSizeLimit: The engine text-rendering size limit for calculator objects.
GraphRenderingSizeLimit: The engine graphical-rendering size limit for calculator objects.
StatsPlotBins: How many bins the engine statistical plot uses. The native Data tool has its own plot workflow.
XYPlotBins: The bin count used by the engine XY plot.
PlotRefreshRate: The refresh interval used by engine plots. It is not the native graph's sample count.
DateSeparatorCommand: The separator in displayed dates. Choose DateSlash, DateDash, DateDot or DateSpace.
MaximumShowWidth: The maximum enlarged calculator-object rendering width in pixels.
MaximumShowHeight: The maximum enlarged calculator-object rendering height in pixels.
EditorWrapColumn: Where calculator program entry wraps. The native SD source editor has its own layout.
TabWidth: The tab width used in calculator rendering, rather than the SD source editor's indentation setting.
ErrorBeepFrequency: The error tone's frequency in Hz. BeepOn/BeepOff separately controls whether calculator sounds are enabled.
ErrorBeepDuration: How long an error tone lasts, in milliseconds.
RandomGeneratorOrder: The engine random-number generator's order parameter. Keep the default unless your RPL work requires another configuration.
RandomGeneratorBits: The bit count used by the engine random-number generator.
ResultFont: The built-in font used for calculator answers. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. This does not resize native Help, menus or source editing.
StackFont: The built-in font used for values on the calculator stack. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. This does not resize native Help, menus or source editing.
EditorFont: The built-in font used for single-line calculator entry. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. This does not resize native Help, menus or source editing.
MultilineEditorFont: The built-in font used for multiline calculator entry. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. This does not resize native Help, menus or source editing.
CursorFont: The built-in font used for the single-line calculator cursor. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. This does not resize native Help, menus or source editing.
MultilineCursorFont: The built-in font used for the multiline calculator cursor. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. This does not resize native Help, menus or source editing.
HeaderFont: The built-in font used for the saved engine header. Font IDs 0-12 are choices, not pixel heights. The PicoCalc header always uses its compact face, so this saved value does not resize it.
